decisions.reason: It remained on the website across 2023 and 2024 and fits the firm's core application equipment business, so a mature medium-sized manufacturer would likely keep it unless sales clearly fall short of aspirations.
Its own product page in both years and the reference to field testing suggest continued commitment and acceptable learning progress, making withdrawal unlikely absent clear underperformance.
Because it stayed on the market and is built around proven WIWA air motors, the product likely benefits from low incremental risk and enough slack to remain in the portfolio.

Although the firm has given it a dedicated page in both years, the lack of visible performance signals makes it somewhat more vulnerable if results disappoint, but not enough to expect an immediate withdrawal.

As a 2024 launch with only limited website presence, it is still in the uncertainty window where a behavioral firm would usually allow time for evaluation, though it faces the highest drop risk if early results miss aspirations.
